newsitem.title: USA: Judge says Klaas killer deserves death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Judge says Klaas killer deserves death penalty.

text.p: A California judge denied two defense motions on Thursday and said Richard Davis deserved the death penalty for the 1993 kidnap and murder of 12-year-old Polly Klaas.

Santa Clara County Superior Court Judge Thomas Hastings denied one defense motion for Davis to be given a new trial on the grounds of juror misconduct and another that the jury's recommended death sentence should be reduced to life imprisonment.
"The court's assessment is that...the evidence in this case as to aggravation is so substantial...and lack of mitigation so obvious that this case warrants the death penalty...," Hastings said.
He ordered a recess to give him time to read the probation department report on Davis and said he would impose sentence when he returned later on Thursday.
Davis, a 42-year-old parolee, was convicted in June of kidnapping and murdering Klaas in a crime that stunned the nation and provoked a campaign to give tougher sentences to repeat offenders.

Davis kidnapped Klaas at knifepoint from a slumber party at her northern California home on October 1, 1993, while her mother slept down the hall. Police said Davis led them to Klaas's body, buried in a shallow grave, two months later.
